denied: ⛔ Access denied. Your ID: {0} Ask the server owner to open the goDNS Pro SSH menu → “Telegram bot” and issue a claim code.
claim_hint: This bot manages goDNS Pro and obeys its admins only. To claim yourself, take the one-time code from the goDNS Pro SSH menu (“Telegram bot” → “Admin claim code”) and send: /start CODE
claim_ok: ✅ Done — you are an admin of this goDNS Pro.
claim_wrong: ✗ Wrong code. The code is one-time: it dies after the first successful use. The SSH menu issues a new one.
claim_closed: The claim code is not active right now. Open the goDNS Pro SSH menu → “Telegram bot” → “Admin claim code”.
claim_expired: ⌛ The code has expired (it lives 15 minutes). Issue a new one in the goDNS Pro SSH menu → “Telegram bot” → “Admin claim code”.
claim_rate_limited: Too many failed attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
claim_already: You are already an admin. Menu: /start
help_text:
Commands:
/start — main menu
/start CODE — claim yourself as admin (code from the SSH menu)
/id — show your Telegram ID
/lang — interface language
/help — this help
main_title: goDNS Pro — encrypted DNS Pick a section:
working_long: ⏳ Working — this may take up to {0} s…
rpc_down: 🔌 The control service (godns-botd) is unreachable. On the server: systemctl status godns-botd
busy: ⏳ Another operation is still running. Wait for it to finish.
timeout_msg: ⏱ Did not finish within {0} s — aborted. Details: server journal.
fail_done: ✗ Finished with an error — details above.
cert_title: Certificate View and renewal hook. Switching or issuing a certificate is done from the goDNS Pro SSH menu: it picks from what is found on the server.
cert_ssh_hint: Change it over SSH: godns → “DNS settings” → “Rescan and choose”.
ups_ssh_hint: Change it over SSH: godns → “DNS settings” → “Rebuild the upstream list”.
ups_custom_limit: The limit of {0} own upstreams is reached — remove one.
cu_proto_title: Own upstream — step 1 of 4: protocol Certificate validation for DoT/DoH is always on: a self-signed one will not work.
cu_addr_ask_dot: Step 2 of 4: address Send the resolver host or IP as a message (host:port is fine).
cu_addr_ask_doh: Step 2 of 4: address Send https://host[:port]/path or just a host (default path /dns-query).
cu_addr_ask_plain: Step 2 of 4: address Send the resolver IP or host (host:port is fine).
cu_addr_bad: Could not parse the address. Expected https://host[:port]/path, host:port or a host. Send it again or press Cancel.
cu_port_ask: Step 3 of 4: port The default for {0} is {1}.
cu_port_type: Send the port number (1–65535) as a message.
cu_port_bad: Port outside 1–65535. Send a number again.
cu_probing: ⏳ Resolving the name and probing the upstream — up to {0} s…
cu_plain_public: ⚠️ Plain DNS to a public address Your clients’ queries will leave for the internet UNENCRYPTED. The ISP and anyone on the path can read them. Continue anyway?
cu_plain_private: The address is private — queries to it stay inside your network.
cu_probe_failed: ✗ Did not answer: {0} You can still add it — in service it will be marked as down.
cu_name_ask: Step 4 of 4: display name Send it as a message (up to 40 characters) or keep the default.
cu_name_bad: Name: up to 40 characters, no | or ;. Send it again.
cu_confirm: Check Protocol: {0} Address: {1} Name: {2} Probe: {3} Put it into the active set right away? The service will reload its configuration.
cu_cancelled: Cancelled — the own upstream was not added.
cu_expired: The input expired (2 minutes) — start over: “Upstreams” → “Add an own upstream”.
cu_rm_in_set: It is in the active set: the service reloads its configuration without it.
cu_rm_not_in_set: It is not in the active set — the service is left alone.
cu_rm_last: This is the only upstream in the active set — pick another one first (SSH: “Rebuild the upstream set”).
ports_ssh_hint: Change it over SSH: godns → “DNS settings” → “Change ports”.
rotate_warn: ⚠️ Rotating the secret DoH path The old address stops working IMMEDIATELY: every configured client loses DNS at once until you hand them the new address. To confirm, send this word as a message: {0}
dot_on_warn:
DoT has no secret path: once enabled it is open to anyone who knows the domain (and the domain is visible in the certificate). It is also the only way to connect Android without apps (port 853).

Enable DoT?
dot_off_warn: Disable DoT? Android clients (Private DNS) will lose DNS.
ext_warn: The third-party service check-host.net will learn your host and port (never the secret DoH path). Continue?
qlog_on_warn: The verbose log writes two lines for EVERY query — at 50 qps that is ~200 MB per hour. It switches itself off on a timer, but the disk is yours. Enable?
svc_stop_warn: Stop dnsdist? Every client loses DNS until the next start.
svc_apply_warn: Apply the current settings and restart the service?
uninstall_warn: ⚠️ Complete goDNS Pro removal Will be removed: the dnsdist service, configuration, renewal hook, timers, goDNS Pro firewall rules and this bot. Will remain: foreign certificates (goVLESS/goTelegram), logs, statistics and backups in /root/godns-backups (a settings backup is taken automatically). To confirm, send this word as a message: {0}
uninstall_bye: goDNS Pro removed. The bot is shutting down — this is its last message.
bk_ssh_hint: Restoring is over SSH: godns → “goDNS Pro settings” → “Restore from a backup”.
